subject: Acceptance Passport: benchmarking evidence exchange and next steps
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Alice Chen <alice@kiteretail.com>, Tom Miller <tom.miller@kiteretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Kickoff: Acceptance Passport and evidence handoff (next steps)

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, we want to run a short "Acceptance Passport" exchange to make the onboarding sign-off as predictable as possible. The goal is to capture a minimal set of artifacts Kite needs for production acceptance (latency/throughput gates, sample telemetry, and a short runbook).

Proposed lightweight plan: 
- Week 1 (this week): Redwood shares acceptance_matrix_v1.xlsx (maps tests to pass/fail thresholds) and a suggested load script.
- Week 2: Kite runs a single daytime load run (~2 hours) against our preprod endpoint and returns the CSV with token-level latencies.
- Week 3: Joint readout and sign-off; finalize SLA draft.

Action items for Kite: confirm target traffic profile (QPS, avg seq length, tail percentile) by EOD Wednesday. We can tailor the load script once we have that.

I've attached the initial acceptance_matrix_v1.xlsx and a short checklist. Monica will own the evidence collection; Ben will help with the test harness.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

—Laura Bennett
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Chen <alice@kiteretail.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Miller <tom.miller@kiteretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Acceptance Passport and evidence handoff (next steps)

Laura — thanks for the clear plan. Confirming Kite's targets here so we line up with your matrix:
- Steady-state QPS: 120 requests/sec
- Average sequence length: 85 tokens
- Target 95th percentile per-token latency: <= 55ms
- Estimated peak batch window: 15 minutes at 180 QPS (simulated burst)

We can have a small infra SME (Tom) run the tests next Tuesday (1/19). We'll upload the CSV and a short note. Can you confirm the preprod endpoint and any auth tokens?

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Chen
Head of Platform, Kite Retail
alice@kiteretail.com
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Kite acceptance targets confirmed (prep for run)

Team — 

Kite confirmed the targets (see Alice's reply). Key items: 120 QPS steady, 180 QPS burst, avg 85 tokens, 95p target 55ms. Please do the following: 
- Monica: prepare the credentials and a dedicated preprod endpoint with a token TTL of 72 hours; include ACL that limits requests to Kite IPs.
- Ben: generate the load script (we'll use the standard rws-load harness) and add per-token timing output; attach a header so we can correlate requests in our telemetry.
- Karthik: please list the model variant we'll pin for the run and confirm quantization/kv-cache behavior so we can document in the passport.

I attached the acceptance matrix for reference. Let's sync for 30m tomorrow (1/13) to hand off artifacts.

—Laura
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-13T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Kite acceptance targets confirmed (prep for run)

On Wed, 2027-01-13, laura_bennett@redwood.com wrote:
> Team — 
> 
> Kite confirmed the targets (see Alice's reply). Key items: 120 QPS steady, 180 QPS burst, avg 85 tokens, 95p target 55ms.

Quick update: load script is ready and I ran a dry smoke run against staging (no client tokens) yesterday. Results (summary):
- Warmed runtime, 120 QPS steady: mean per-token latency 34ms, 95p 48ms
- Burst test at 180 QPS (15m): 95p climbed to 62ms for a ~3-minute window then recovered

I'll attach the full CSV from the staging smoke ("load_results_20270118.csv") once we do the Kite run. I'm adding a small retry/backoff in the harness to reduce transient tail spikes — this will be optional for Kite to enable.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@kiteretail.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Miller <tom.miller@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T14:28:00-08:00
Subject: Kite run results and artifacts (upload)

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks for running the test this morning. I've uploaded the CSV and a short evidence packet to the Drive link in the thread. Quick summary of Kite's run: 
- Run window: 2027-01-18 09:00–11:00 PT (steady 120 QPS, burst 180 QPS at 10:10)
- Observed 95p per-token latency: 52ms during steady, peaked to 68ms during the 3-min burst spike
- Error rate: 0.01% (3 HTTP 503s during burst window, linked in CSV)

Attachments: load_results_20270118.csv (column headers: ts,req_id,token_idx,token_latency_ms,status_code)

Next steps: 
1) We recommend a short joint readout on 1/20 to review the CSV and decide on SLA language for burst handling (DocuSign link in related_links).
2) If Kite wants mitigations, Ben can demo a per-route cache warm and retry policy that reduces short-duration tail spikes.

Link to artifacts: https://drive.redwood/company/onboarding/KD-4821/acceptance_passport (access granted to kite external users)

—Monica
Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Chen <alice@kiteretail.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Miller <tom.miller@redwood.com>, Kite Retail Procurement <procurement@kiteretail.com>
Date: 2027-01-20T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance Passport: benchmarking evidence exchange and next steps

Thanks — we reviewed the CSV and the readout this afternoon. High level: pass for steady-state; the short burst spike is acceptable if we get an operational note in the SLA describing tolerance and remediation steps.

We propose the following SLA language (short): "95th-percentile per-token latency <= 60ms for steady-state up to 150 QPS. Short-duration bursts up to 200 QPS are covered with an operational tolerance up to 10% above the 95p target for a contiguous 5-minute window; Redwood will provide mitigation guidance and a runbook for repeatable spikes."

Tom and procurement are good to receive a redline of the SLA doc; Alice will loop legal if needed. Please send the DocuSign link when the SLA draft is ready.

Best,
Alice
